case_label_entity_level: Donor (putative class) v. Schwab Charitable Fund et al.
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
defendant_entities_and_roles: Schwab Charitable Fund; Charles Schwab & Co.; Schwab Charitable board of directors; Schwab Charitable investment oversight committee
outcome: Affirmed: no Article III standing; court did not reach California statutory standing. One judge concurred in part and in the judgment, and would hold reputational/expressive injuries from DAF spending never confer standing
key_holding_quote: "Because Pinkert has no right to control how Schwab Charitable invests or donates the funds he contributed, and he does not allege that the right he does have—the right to provide nonbinding advice—was infringed, his property-rights-based theory of standing fails too." Concurrence: "the common law has long disallowed donors from suing charities for the alleged mismanagement of fully relinquished charitable donations, leaving oversight of charities and the enforcement of charitable trusts to the state Attorneys General."
pin_cite: slip op. 12 (majority); slip op. 16 (concurrence); see also slip op. 6 (sponsor 'not legally obligated to comply with the donor's advice')
evidence_grade: P (slip opinion read from court CDN; govinfo package metadata confirms date and caption)
notes: Repo cites the reporter citation 48 F.4th 1051; not re-verified here (FindLaw robots 403). Repo LIT-02 gave the decision month only (2022-09); the slip opinion is dated 2022-09-14. Concurrence cites Herbst v. Univ. of Colo. Found., 513 P.3d 388 (Colo. Ct. App. 2022) (donor status insufficient for standing; not a DAF case), relevant to the Colorado Peterson case.

category: tax: DAF acknowledgment and exclusive legal control
court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas (Dallas)
filed_date: 2020 (year from docket number; exact date not verified)

claims: Tax refund for 2015 after IRS disallowed deduction for donating a 4% hotel LP interest to a DAF at The Pi Fund

notes: Refund claims denied were $507964.80 (Claim 1); alternatives $327520.00 and $136875.00 (Doc. 79 at 34). Final judgment entered 2022-07-07 (Doc. 86 at 2).
